name: Ossian Perforated Moto Jacket
description:
A fitted motorcycle jacket in full-grain cowhide, black with a slight pull-up finish that shows the leather's natural character under light. The cut is asymmetric-zip, with a wide lapel that can be snapped closed at the throat, perforated panels across the shoulders and upper sleeves for airflow, and four exterior pockets — two slash at the hip, one zip at the chest, one welt at the collar. The lining is a slick viscose in deep burgundy. No padding, no armor, no tech. Just a very good leather jacket.

Ossian is a Tier 3 independent, one of a handful of labels still doing genuine leather goods in GLMZ. They source from synthetic-free ranches in the Wisconsin interior and tan in small batches. The perforated moto has been in their line for fifteen years with minimal changes because nothing about it needs changing. It's the kind of jacket that looks better at forty hours than it does at zero.
what_it_says: You have personal style that didn't come from an algorithm. You understand quality and you're willing to pay for it without needing to tell anyone.
story_hooks: Ossian's leather supplier has gone dark — three weeks without contact, and the last shipment arrived with a hide that had been branded with a mark no one at Ossian recognizes.
A specific Ossian moto jacket keeps appearing in security footage across three districts over six months — always in the background, always in motion, never showing the wearer's face.

A Tier 5 collector is paying absurd premiums for first-run Ossian pieces, claiming they contain trace compounds from an extinct tanning process — the current owners of those jackets have no idea why they're suddenly targets.

physical_description.visual_profile: A classic fitted moto silhouette with asymmetric swagger—sharp lapels, nipped waist, athletic shoulders. The perforated panels across the shoulders and upper sleeves create deliberate negative space that reads as aggressive ventilation and raw craft. Worn-in character is built into the material's DNA. Sits somewhere between vintage rebel and contemporary minimalist.
physical_description.fit: Fitted through the chest and torso with a slight taper at the waist. Sleeves are tapered but mobile. Lapels are wide and structured, designed to fold close or snap open. Not restrictive—built for movement on a bike or walking a warehouse floor.
physical_description.primary_material: Full-grain cowhide with pull-up finish—leather that develops a patina and color depth naturally over time. No synthetics, no shortcuts. Wisconsin-sourced, small-batch tanned.
physical_description.texture: Smooth but tactile, with visible grain variation. The pull-up finish creates subtle creasing and darkening under pressure and light. Perforated panels are clean-edged, not rough. Viscose lining feels slick against skin—warm burgundy that catches light.
physical_description.color_scheme: Black leather that pulls to deep brown in creases and under UV. Deep burgundy viscose interior. Matte hardware in brushed steel or aged silver.
physical_description.closures: Asymmetric front zip (offset, not center), snap throat closure at the wide lapel, four functional pockets—two hip slashes, one chest zip, one collar welt. No unnecessary hardware.
distinctive_features: Perforated shoulder and upper-sleeve panels—functional airflow aesthetic
Asymmetric zip with snap throat closure—sharp design detail
Pull-up leather that develops character with wear—patina over time
Minimal branding—Ossian mark subtle or absent
Slick burgundy viscose lining—unexpected interior luxury
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 Independent—not corpo luxury, but honest craft. Price point suggests skilled working professional or salvage-turned-legitimate operator. Signals investment in durability, not status.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by: street mechanics, independent couriers, makers and craftspeople, vintage-conscious rebels, anyone who rejects fast-fashion cycle. Says 'I buy things that last and look better broken in.' No corpo pretense, no sub-grade salvage—clean lineage.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine on purchase, but built to be worn hard. After 40+ hours: leather shows natural creasing, perforated areas darken slightly, sleeves develop character at the cuffs. After a year: rich patina, deep color variation, scuffs that read as story, not damage.
